body:
There exists an integration test for 2D arrays, but it is targetting a test template with two parameters:

https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/blob/master/junit-jupiter-params/src/test/java/org/junit/jupiter/params/ParameterizedTestIntegrationTests.java#L319-L327

And this is the output of the above workaround:

```
[[1, 2]]
[[2, 3]]
```

> ....yields:
> 
> ```
> class [I -> [I@8e0379d = [1, 2]
> class [I -> [I@161b062a = [2, 3]
> ```

Right, but... that is still producing a one-dimensional array.

The issue is that a multi-dimensional array is passed to `Arguments.of(Object...)` **without** casting it to an `(Object)` like in my workaround.

So the var-args support _removes_ the enclosing array, resulting in a one-dimensional array.

In case you want to see that... it happens here:

https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/blob/685c14dffa50f04e304cc305ad5ee9a5a36a33ba/junit-jupiter-params/src/main/java/org/junit/jupiter/params/provider/MethodArgumentsProvider.java#L86-L94

FYI: It's the final return statement.

body:
FWIW, my _fix_ on the feature branch does in fact support the failing use case described in this issue.

However, it also brings to light some oddities with regard to support for Object and primitive arrays.

1. If you have a factory method that returns `Stream<Object[]>`, that will **NOT** allow you to have a `@ParameterizedTest` method that accepts a single `Object[]` argument.
   - Rather, if the lengths of the arrays are at least 2, that would require a `@ParameterizedTest` method with a signature of `test(Object, Object)`, `test(String, int)`, or similar.
2. If you have a factory method that returns `Stream<int[]>`, that **WILL** allow you to have a `@ParameterizedTest` method that accepts a single `int[]` argument.
   - And that was the case before my _fix_.

> I am attempting to pass two-dimensional arrays of primitives to a parameterized test. The one-dimensional array works as expected,

@junit-team/junit-lambda, this is one of the points we need to decide on: what is actually "expected" here with regard to the previous points I made.
